Manu is a new cafe in Artiaga Street, and it’s quite easy to miss because there isn’t a big sign outside yet. The space itself is nice. It’s modern, aesthetic, well-lit, and clean. Their coffee and matcha were good, and they offer oat milk as a substitute. They also have a small selection of finger food and pasta. I also like that they open early at 7 AM and close late at 10 PM. They don’t have wifi but there are plenty of sockets around the cafe if you need to charge your devices. One downside during my visit was that there were a few flies inside the cafe. I mentioned it to the staff and they brought out a candle. It would’ve made the experience much better if there weren’t any flies, because the place really has a lot of potential. They currently accept cash and QR payments only, and they don’t have a sales invoice. Parking was a bit confusing at first. I thought it was street parking only, but apparently there’s a parking lot beside the cafe. Some signage for that would help. The staff were able to assist when needed, though a bit more warmth in service would make the experience even nicer. Overall, it’s a promising cafe with good drinks and a nice atmosphere. With a few small improvements, it could easily become a favorite spot in the neighborhood.

Manu Coffee Davao has quickly become one of my favorite spots in the city and I’ve only been twice! The ambience is cozy and well thought out, the kind of place you actually want to linger in. Their food is genuinely good too, the carbonara, bolognese, and salad all hit. I love their matcha oat, and of course, the coffee delivers. The staff are warm and organized, which really ties the whole experience together. Super quick serving too. Another thing I liked is that even tho the place is puno ng tao you wont even feel the noise. If you’re in Davao, this one’s worth the visit. Highly recommend! ☕✨
